definitions.gloss: stroll; ramble; leisurely walk without a destination
definitions.explanation: Walking around aimlessly and at a relaxed pace, enjoying the surroundings rather than heading toward a specific goal. A somewhat literary word.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}の{公園|こうえん}を{漫歩|まんぽ}した。
examples.english: I took a leisurely walk through the park in autumn.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}を{忘|わす}れて{異国|いこく}の{路地|ろじ}を{漫歩|まんぽ}するのが、{旅|たび}の{醍醐味|だいごみ}だ。
examples.english: The real pleasure of travel is forgetting about work and strolling through foreign alleyways.

notes:
Composed of {漫|まん} (aimless, rambling) + {歩|ぽ} (walk, step). A literary and somewhat refined word for walking without purpose.

USAGE:
{漫歩|まんぽ} is used primarily in written language — essays, travel writing, and literary descriptions. In everyday conversation, {散歩|さんぽ} or ぶらぶら{歩|ある}く are more natural. {漫歩|まんぽ} emphasizes the aimless, unhurried quality of the walk more than {散歩|さんぽ} does.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {街|まち}を{漫歩|まんぽ}する: to stroll through a town
- {漫歩|まんぽ}を{楽|たの}しむ: to enjoy a stroll
- {都市|とし}{漫歩|まんぽ}: urban strolling
- {漫歩|まんぽ}{記|き}: rambling notes, strolling diary

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {散歩|さんぽ}: walk, stroll — the everyday word for taking a walk; can be purposeful (exercise, dog walking) or leisurely
- {散策|さんさく}: leisurely walk, exploring on foot — similar in register to {漫歩|まんぽ}, but implies more active looking around and exploring
- ぶらぶら{歩|ある}く: to wander around — casual, conversational expression for aimless walking
